commit.subject: [dawn] Use `std::countl_zero()` in C++20
commit.message:
[dawn] Use `std::countl_zero()` in C++20

This patch always uses the function `std::countl_zero()` (counting
the number of consecutive zeros starting from the most significant
bit) instead of the equivalent ones that are platform-dependent
(e.g. `_BitScanForward()` on Windows, `__builtin_clz()` in GCC).

This patch also removes `dawn::ScanReverse()` as it is no longer
used right now.

Bug: 343500108

[dawn] Use `std::countl_zero()` in C++20

This patch always uses the function `std::countl_zero()` (counting
the number of consecutive zeros starting from the most significant
bit) instead of the equivalent ones that are platform-dependent
(e.g. `_BitScanForward()` on Windows, `__builtin_clz()` in GCC).

This patch also removes `dawn::ScanReverse()` as it is no longer
used right now.

commit.subject: D3D11: fix SystemEventQueue's incorrect tracking of completed serials
commit.message:
D3D11: fix SystemEventQueue's incorrect tracking of completed serials

SystemEventQueue currently recycles events in 2 places:
- CheckAndUpdateCompletedSerials().
- WaitForQueueSerial().

This leads to incorrect update of the completed serial in
CheckAndUpdateCompletedSerials().

Considering the following scenario:
- Queue.Submit() is called 2 times.
  - SystemEventQueue will store a pending list of event 1 & 2 associated
  with serial 1 & 2.
- WaitQueueSerials(serial=1, timeout=inf) is called.
  - WaitForQueueSerial() is called.
    - This waits until serial=1 is completed.
    - Event 1 will be removed from the pending list.
  - CheckAndUpdateCompletedSerials() is called.
    - This function attempts to check the status of all pending events.
    - Event 2 is the only one in the pending list at this point.
    - If the event 2 was not signaled yet, the function would return
    GetCompletedCommandSerial() which is zero. Because the actual
    completed serial=1 has not been notified to the parent Queue class
    yet.

This CL fixes the bug by removing the recylcing from
WaitForQueueSerial(). Only CheckAndUpdateCompletedSerials() should
recycle the events. Because it's the place supposed to update the
completed serial.

Bug: 415561579
Change-Id: Ifb9fca831a5ccb7bfc165641179966a6bc4a6203

commit.subject: [tint][ir][fuzz] Assert that HLSL `Generate()` succeeds
commit.message:
[tint][ir][fuzz] Assert that HLSL `Generate()` succeeds

Currently the HLSL fuzzer assums that if `CanGenerate()` succeeds then
`Generate()` will pass also, which this test proves is not true.

This CL adds in a check on the result of `Generate()` so that the
crash report is at the earliest possible time it can be detected,
instead of later failing in the call to DXC.

Bug: 415190405
Change-Id: If052aeee30ff5cce26fbe5797a0b693315f5e7fb

commit.subject: Pre-cache all JNI class lookups
commit.message:
Pre-cache all JNI class lookups

A new class JNIClasses created to hold all the class references.

A singleton is held by the existing JNIContext object.

This should aid performance and also is needed for cross-thread
JNI access e.g. in callbacks.

commit.subject: Pre-cache all JNI class lookups
commit.message:
Pre-cache all JNI class lookups

A new class JNIClasses created to hold all the class references.

This is needed for cross-thread JNI access e.g. in callbacks, as
'env' objects can only partially be shared across threads, e.g.
they cannot be used for FindClass. The cache may also improve
performance.

Sadly this cannot be held by the existing JNIContext object
because that has already been destroyed when the callback
happens.

Bug: 341889978
Test: Exercised by ./gradlew connectedAndroidTest
Change-Id: I99b490d9a5f94efff5eeaadfbf5529976153d728

commit.subject: Add BitSetRangeIterator
commit.message:
Add BitSetRangeIterator

Add a new iterator for Dawn BitSet. The iterator defines "range". "range" means
continuous set bits and represents with [offset, size] pair.

The new iterator iterate between ranges and could help immediate data states
tracker to do state tracking.

commit.message:
[tint][ir][fuzz] Re-enable generating the IR corpus

This uncomments the related action and sets its dependencies to make
sure that they are built for the host toolchain where they will be
invoked. The generation action is removed as a depenency for the
fuzzer, since it takes a long time to run and we don't want to pay
that cost on every build.

commit.subject: [tint][ir][val] Handle names for builtins without checkers
commit.message:
[tint][ir][val] Handle names for builtins without checkers

In `CheckFunctionReturnAttributesAndType` the name of the builtin is
included in the error message, which is normally fetched from the
associated `BuiltinChecker`.

For some builtins there is no checker defined, since the logic
required to validate it is more complex than what that framework
allows, which causes an ICE.

These builtins need to be handled as special cases, as-is done when
validating builtins in general.

Fixes: 414728882
Change-Id: Icd6794d7a4d415014ff311b6b496827352414a00

[tint][ir][val] Handle names for builtins without checkers

In `CheckFunctionReturnAttributesAndType` the name of the builtin is
included in the error message, which is normally fetched from the
associated `BuiltinChecker`.

For some builtins there is no checker defined, since the logic
required to validate it is more complex than what that framework
allows, which causes an ICE.

These builtins need to be handled as special cases, as-is done when
validating builtins in general.

Fixes: 414728882
Change-Id: Icd6794d7a4d415014ff311b6b496827352414a00
Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/239874
Commit-Queue: Ryan Harrison <rharrison@chromium.org>
Auto-Submit: Ryan Harrison <rharrison@chromium.org>
Reviewed-by: dan sinclair <dsinclair@chromium.org>

commit.message:
Fix 'absl' targets for is_component_build

The upstream version of this BUILD.gn has the target as a `component`
target, which is a chromium //build specific thing, so cannot be used
in stand alone Skia.

Instead for the Dawn custom version it is will be a `source set` and
not include macros/defs related to component builds which were
breaking Windows specific builds.

Fixes: 409589680

commit.subject: Ensure WGSL StringView knows length
commit.message:
Ensure WGSL StringView knows length

When ShaderModule passes WGSL string it first converts to const char*
and then StringView. This discards length information and requires
strlen() to be used to figure out length again later. Don't discard the
length information to avoid this.

Bug: none
Change-Id: I910a2680f3e373049f211f2a1f19c06a9e789a14

commit.subject: [spirv] Fix construct for subgroup matrix composites
commit.message:
[spirv] Fix construct for subgroup matrix composites

Zero-value constructors are not folded into constants when the type
contains a subgroup matrix.

We already special-cased this scenario to emit OpConstantNull for
non-composite subgroup matrix types, so do the same for composites

commit.subject: Remove ConcurrentTransformedShaderModuleCache
commit.message:
Remove ConcurrentTransformedShaderModuleCache

ConcurrentTransformedShaderModuleCache held both compiled SPIR-V and
VkShaderModule. There is already caching of SPIR-V in BlobCache. The
transformation from SPIR-V to VkShaderModule is inexpensive. This extra
layer of caching isn't really necessary so remove it.

Render/compute pipeline now call vkDestroyShaderModule() after
compilation is complete. This also removes the need for FencedDeleter to
handle that.

Bug: 411152029
Change-Id: Ia75f313849a5bade092f2a99d608cceb76a1b3c4

commit.message:
Make git-cl format Python by default

Turns out we don't need to type git cl format --python every time. If we
just add a .style.yapf file (per git cl format --help) it will do it by
default.

Remove check_python=True from PRESUBMIT.py so that it will also choose
automatically based on the presence of .style.yapf - and suggest `git cl
format` instead of `git cl format --python` when running presubmit
checks on `git cl upload` or `git cl presubmit`.

commit.subject: Make git-cl not need --python to format Python
commit.message:
Make git-cl not need --python to format Python

Turns out we don't need to type git cl format --python every time. If we
add a .style.yapf file, it will do it by default. git cl format --help:

> If neither --python or --no-python are set, python files that have a
> .style.yapf file in an ancestor directory will be formatted.

Remove check_python=True from PRESUBMIT.py so that it will also choose
automatically based on the presence of .style.yapf - and suggest `git cl
format` instead of `git cl format --python` when running checks during
`git cl upload` or `git cl presubmit`. presubmit_canned_checks.py:

> Explicitly setting check_python to will enable/disable python formatting
> on all files. Leaving it as None will enable checking patch formatting
> on files that have a .style.yapf file in a parent directory.

Bug: none
Change-Id: Ia22f783b30181bed54933c732749a9837837bac2

commit.subject: Specialized bitset iterator depending on size
commit.message:
Specialized bitset iterator depending on size

Begins work to specialize the ityp::bitset iterator depending on the
size of the bitset. Currently only supports the previous any-sized
iterator, used for large bitsets, and a 64-bit iterator used for any
bitset with less than 64 elements.

The bitset itself is largely unchanged, and still based on std::bitset
in all cases.

Bug: 42241557
Change-Id: Ic17a1ae9a10a98479199eb9fc84cb63170d7a5e6

commit.subject: Request contents:write permission for GitHub release workflow
commit.message:
Request contents:write permission for GitHub release workflow

The 'google' org on GitHub is configured so that the default
GITHUB_TOKEN permission for Actions is read-only. So we need to specify
which write permissions we need for the action so it can upload a
release.

Verified on my personal fork by changing the config to match 'google'.
It fails to upload a release before this fix, and succeeds after.

No-Try: true
Bug: 371024051
Change-Id: I86a772b73aaaf9984235d05215e755c777733642

commit.message:
Dawn: Use EP name with isolation key hash in backend shader code

This CL make generated backend shader code use secure entry point name
containing hash of device isolation key (if provided) for all backends
except OpenGL. GLSL requires the EP name being "main".

commit.subject: D3D11: Always use custom device context state.
commit.message:
D3D11: Always use custom device context state.

Currently we only use a custom device context state when we share the
D3D11 device. We swap in & activate it during render pass, compute pass'
executions. The purpose is to avoid Dawn messing up the D3D state of
other modules such as ANGLE, video decoder, etc.

However, this makes the behavior inconsistent between tests and chrome
use cases which share the D3D11 device.

This CL forces D3D11 backend to always use the custom device context
state. It will make the tests easier.

Bug: 413000772
Change-Id: I1baaa4f30919d699f5c0fba82b9b3a769a812a3c

commit.subject: D3D11: fix internal uniform buffer's binding not persistent.
commit.message:
D3D11: fix internal uniform buffer's binding not persistent.

In D3D11 backend we create and bind an internal uniform buffer once at
initialization time. However, at that point, the custom D3D11 device
context state is not active yet. Hence when we activate it using
ScopedSwapStateCommandRecordingContext during render pass & compute pass
executions, that binding would be lost. This leads to shaders reading
invalid data from an unbound buffer. D3D will return zeros in this case.

Fix it by binding the internal uniform buffer using
ScopedSwapStateCommandRecordingContext which automatically activates the
custom D3D11 device context state.

Note that this bug is currently not detected by end2end tests because
the custom D3D device context state is only used when Dawn shares D3D
device with other modules such as ANGLE, video decoder, etc. In future,
we should always use custom device context state even if the D3D device
is not shared. That would make the behaviors consistent.

Bug: 413000772
Change-Id: I572e718e0b0c2bd8452fc5d0d331aae2b96894c7

commit.subject: Fix activate-emsdk for Linux
commit.message:
Fix activate-emsdk for Linux

We unset PYTHON to make sure we don't use the SDK version of Python in
Dawn builds. But it turns out that was only set on some platforms, not
including Linux, so this failed on the GitHub action.

Other parts of the Dawn build don't seem to care about which version of
Python they use (e.g. DEPS hooks and dawn_json_generator.py just use the
system-installed python3). Unsetting it should also use the
system-installed version. But there's no particular reason to bother
avoiding the version that emsdk gets for us.

So, just leave it as emsdk sets it.

Bug: 371024051
Change-Id: I34a206467395de4515182fded6ec63068353f864

commit.subject: Remove Node/LLVM overrides from activate-emsdk
commit.message:
Remove Node/LLVM overrides from activate-emsdk

We only use emsdk as a toolchain to build a emdawnwebgpu_pkg, samples,
and tests, so it isn't important to override the Node and LLVM binary
paths to use the ones Dawn uses. It's a bit fragile/incomplete (our LLVM
releases don't include binaries that Emscripten needs; the LLVM version
could mismatch; etc.) so it's easiest to just remove for now. We can
bring it back later if needed.

This also obsoletes a bug in activate-emsdk on Linux where PYTHON wasn't
set, so `del PYTHON` didn't work.

Bug: 371024051
Change-Id: I34a206467395de4515182fded6ec63068353f864

commit.subject: [dawn][wire] Fix dawn wire server to use ProcessEvents.
commit.message:
[dawn][wire] Fix dawn wire server to use ProcessEvents.

- The wire server should currently (by default) be using
  ProcessEvents for most callbacks. Otherwise, it's possible
  for races since the wire is not currently thread safe.
- Note that requestAdapter and requestDevice are currently
  exceptions.
- In the future, once the wire is thread-safe, we should be
  able to forward the callback mode accordingly instead of
  forcing all wire server callbacks to be ProcessEvents.

Change-Id: I4d3c4ff282ffa224606806586a5b2956737bfae8

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Handle UserCall atomic convertions.
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Handle UserCall atomic convertions.

When processing `UserCall` instructions for atomic conversions we may
need to fork the called functions. In order to fork, we have to collect
up all of the parameters which become atomics in that specific user call
and make a custom forked function. We store this combination of
(function, parameters converted) so we only fork the function one for
each combination of argument.

Bug: 404501988
Change-Id: I6bd318151d9e611ffae038b14c4598606f48a3ef

commit.subject: Publish emdawnwebgpu in a GitHub release
commit.message:
Publish emdawnwebgpu in a GitHub release

This runs a github action which:
- Builds emdawnwebgpu_pkg
- Saves the version info into emdawnwebgpu_pkg/VERSION.txt
- Zips emdawnwebgpu_pkg
- Creates a git tag vYYYY.MM.DD
- Creates a release for that tag with emdawnwebgpu_pkg-VERSION.zip

If triggered manually, the tag and release name will be
vYYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS instead.

If someday we publish additional build artifacts, they can be published
as additional files in the same release, alongside this one (e.g. native
binaries, or CMake configs that automatically select between Dawn and
emdawnwebgpu based on build target).

Note the Git tags will be created via the GitHub API (they are required
in order to publish releases on GitHub). I don't know yet whether these
will get synced into googlesource.com (or if the sync will try to delete
the tags since they don't exist there - I think GitHub will prevent
that, but that could cause the sync to stop working).

Bug: 371024051
Change-Id: I59683a8ec40e0db940e35c9e1ea8c7e678686977

commit.subject: [emscripten] Build a packageable directory for emdawnwebgpu
commit.message:
[emscripten] Build a packageable directory for emdawnwebgpu

This creates a new output directory `emdawnwebgpu_pkg` in the build
root. This contains exactly the files needed to link emdawnwebgpu,
and a CMakeLists.txt file that can be included via add_subdirectory
(or just as a reference for how to link the bindings).

This could probably be done more "properly" using an "install" target;
CMake seems to have features for autogenerating packageable .cmake
files, etc. However "install" doesn't support dependencies, so it builds
everything, including a bunch of Tint stuff that's buildable with
Emscripten but irrelevant to emdawnwebgpu, and there's no way to avoid
that. Plus this feels much easier to understand, at least for now.

Bug: 371024051
Change-Id: I60e0883ce0e44be9413dca1439cdb30382571cdf

[emscripten] Build a packageable directory for emdawnwebgpu

This creates a new output directory `emdawnwebgpu_pkg` in the build
root. This contains exactly the files needed to link emdawnwebgpu,
and a CMakeLists.txt file that can be included via add_subdirectory
(or just as a reference for how to link the bindings).

This could probably be done more "properly" using an "install" target;
CMake seems to have features for autogenerating packageable .cmake
files, etc. However "install" doesn't support dependencies, so it builds
everything, including a bunch of Tint stuff that's buildable with
Emscripten but irrelevant to emdawnwebgpu, and there's no way to avoid
that. I'm also unsure whether any of that would work given that we are
trying to distribute webgpu.cpp as a source file, not a prebuilt binary.
Regardless, this feels much easier to understand, at least for now.

Bug: 371024051
Change-Id: I60e0883ce0e44be9413dca1439cdb30382571cdf

commit.subject: [emscripten] Build a packageable directory for emdawnwebgpu
commit.message:
[emscripten] Build a packageable directory for emdawnwebgpu

This creates a new output directory `emdawnwebgpu_pkg` in the build
root. This contains exactly the files needed to link emdawnwebgpu,
and a `port.py` file that can be used via `emcc --use-port=`a.

Instructions on how to use the port are in `port.py`.

The structure of the output directory in the out/*/ directory is:

emdawnwebgpu_pkg
├── include_c
│   └── webgpu
│       └── webgpu.h
├── include_cpp
│   ├── dawn
│   │   └── webgpu_cpp_print.h
│   └── webgpu
│       ├── webgpu_cpp_chained_struct.h
│       ├── webgpu_cpp.h
│       └── webgpu_enum_class_bitmasks.h
├── LICENSE
├── port.py
└── src
    ├── library_webgpu_enum_tables.js
    ├── library_webgpu_generated_sig_info.js
    ├── library_webgpu_generated_struct_info.js
    ├── library_webgpu.js
    ├── webgpu-externs.js
    └── webgpu.cpp

Bug: 371024051
Change-Id: I60e0883ce0e44be9413dca1439cdb30382571cdf

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Error on mixed atomic Min/Max calls.
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Error on mixed atomic Min/Max calls.

In SPIR-V it's permitted to call an `OpAtomicU{Min,Max}` on signed
values, and `OpAtomicS{Min,Max}` on unsigned values. The min/max
operations happen as the type of the call, but there is no way to
represent this in WGSL, we'd end up doing the min/max in the type of the
arguments.

Assert that the argument type matches the call name in the SPIR-V
reader.

Bug: 406565362
Change-Id: Ic73176e120cc0562cc22728d80df7963a954234a

commit.subject: Add VulkanAddWorkToEmptyResolvePass Toggle
commit.message:
Add VulkanAddWorkToEmptyResolvePass Toggle

This toggle is enabled by default on Qualcomm GPUs and adds a small
amount of work (a timestamp write) to render passes which contain no
draw commands. This works around a driver bug where the resolve targets
of the empty pass don't get resolved.

This case is covered by the CTS with
https://gpuweb.github.io/cts/standalone/?runnow=1&q=webgpu:api,operation,render_pass,resolve:render_pass_resolve:*
which was observed to fail on a Pixel 4 but with this fix now passes.

Bug: 411656647
Change-Id: If89e57df5289e18cf7314a9025d2ac985792ba8f

parents.subject: [dawn][native] Support BG with BGLs that use arraySize.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Add Compatibility between BGLEArraySize and binding_array
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Add Compatibility between BGLEArraySize and binding_array

This adds reflection of the array size of the WGSL bindings in
EntryPointMetadata. The compatibility check with the BGL is updated to
require the arraySize to be big enough.

The pipeline defaulting is also updated to make a BGLEArraySize when
needed.

Tests are added.

Bug: 393558555
Change-Id: I77e1ad908cd0cc48a9e54a94e2beb004f40079c8

parents.subject: [dawn][native] Cleanup BGL creation to better support arraySize

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Support BG with BGLs that use arraySize.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Support BG with BGLs that use arraySize.

This expands the single BGL entry at the API surface into one
BindingInfo per element in the BGL's internal format. This lets BG
validation and code to store element unchanged. A test is added that one
must specify all the array elements when creating a BG with a BGL that
uses arraySize.

BGL validation is updated to require that elements created for the
arrays never go past maxBindingsPerBindGroup, and a test is added.

Bug: 393558555
Change-Id: I7e91040d7659d4db26bc1b46a38aef08e707be0c

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Cleanup BGL creation to better support arraySize
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Cleanup BGL creation to better support arraySize

Support for arraySize needs to update ExtractAndExpandBglEntries in
awkward ways because that method and other related code had accumulated
debt. Refactor it a bit in preparation for arraySize.

 - Separate the binding counts used to iterate the BGL from the ones
   used for the validation of total binding counts in the pipeline
   layouts. Extra bindings are accounted for in BindingCounts for
   currently unused ExternalTexture reserved resources (one sampler and
   two sampled textures) and the confusion could cause subtle bugs in
   the future.
 - Change ExtractAndExpandBglEntries to do the conversion to BindingInfo
   internally, which avoids the need to store a linked list of
   BindGroupLayoutEntry on the side. Rename it to
   ConvertAndExpandBGLEntries.
 - Make it return all of its results by value instead of a mix with
   pointers (also go down from 6 things returned to only 2).
 - Update SortBindingsCompare to work with BindingInfo and simplify the
   logic to only what is needed to get the invariants that BGL requires.
 - Make the various *BindingLayout aggregate types by removing their
   constructors and using a static ::From member function instead.
 - Move operator == and != to BindingInfo instead of having it defined
   in BindGroupLayoutInternal.h
 - Remove / inline a couple unused BindGroupLayoutInternal member
   functions.

Bug: 393558555
Change-Id: Idc5365b61460a51ed30d6e829b37dcb05ebd76e5

commit.subject: Reland "Reland "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent""
commit.message:
Reland "Reland "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent""

This is a reland of commit a218ceac197ff55273d80942e114eea9d6dcc90c

The only substantive change over the original is that we release the
waiterLock before iterating through the events at the end so that TSAN
doesn't get tripped up by the benign lock order inversion between
SyncWaiter::mutex and WaitListEvent::mMutex.

Original change's description:
> Reland "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent"
>
> This is a reland of commit abc42736ef28ed8fcc11e66814907febff6ee930
>
> The only change over the original is the correct initialization of the
> `mSignaled` atomic_bool in WaitListEvent.
>
> Original change's description:
> > [ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent
> >
> > Currently, most futures are implemented using SystemEvent. This includes
> > already completed and non-progressing events. This is problematic on iOS
> > where BrowserEngineKit child processes are not allowed to open fds, mach
> > ports, etc.
> >
> > This CL introduces WaitListEvent which mimics the base::WaitableEvent
> > implementation in Chromium for POSIX platforms. The event internally
> > maintains a list of waiters corresponding to a WaitAny call. In WaitAny,
> > we create a SyncWaiter that's signaled using a condition variable. The
> > waiter is added to each event that the WaitAny is waiting on. The events
> > also have a mutex to allow multiple threads to wait on them. We acquire
> > the event locks in a globally consistent order (sorted by address) to
> > prevent lock order inversion. WaitListEvents can also be waited on
> > asynchronously by returning a SystemEventReceiver which allows mixing
> > waits on SystemEvents and WaitListEvents.
> >
> > In addition, this CL changes how already signaled and non-progressing
> > TrackedEvents are represented. Already signaled events are backed by
> > WaitListEvents and non-progressing events become a flag on TrackedEvent.
> >
> > The code in EventManager is also cleaned up to aid readability and fix
> > an edge case of waiting on multiple queues with zero timeout - we could
> > end up ticking the same queue multiple times causing a subtle race
> > between MapAsync and OnSubmittedWorkDone futures completion.
> >
> > Bug: 407801085

commit.message:
Range Analysis: Compute the range of loop control variable - Part II

This patch implements the range analysis on the loop control variable
of a simple for-loop when the for-loop matches the below pattern:

```
// The range of i is [const_value, const_rhs - 1]
for (var i = const_value; i < const_rhs; i++)

// The range of i is [const_rhs + 1, const_value]
for (var i = const_value; i > const_rhs; i--)
```

commit.message:
Reland "Dawn: Use no Tint Program at all in shader compilation cache checking"

This reverts commit 22ee238376b8b5be900c802598e6e2514547ad37.

Reason for revert: 

The right-shifting rhs not less than bits of lhs issue that cause the roll into Skia failed should be fixed by https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/237874.

Bug: 402772740, 402772408
Original change's description:
> Revert "Dawn: Use no Tint Program at all in shader compilation cache checking"
>
> This reverts commit 7fcdc9036915542a08d5b213bb717fea33a125ef.
>
> Reason for revert: This broke the roll into Skia due to UB caused by a right-shift of 64 in the Rotl function:
> https://logs.chromium.org/logs/skia/705dbe4282a5c611/+/steps/dm/0/stdout
>
> Bug: 402772740, 402772408

> > Dawn: Use no Tint Program at all in shader compilation cache checking
> >
> > This CL remove Tint Program from all backends' shader compilation cache
> > key and replace it with SHA3-512 hash of shader module. With this CL,
> > Tint Program might not be need until actual cache miss in backend shader

commit.subject: Revert "Reland "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent""
commit.message:
Revert "Reland "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent""

This reverts commit a218ceac197ff55273d80942e114eea9d6dcc90c.

Reason for revert: Linux TSAN failures in WaitListEventTests:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Dawn%20Linux%20TSAN%20Release/60645/overview

Bug: 407801085
Original change's description:
> Reland "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent"
>
> This is a reland of commit abc42736ef28ed8fcc11e66814907febff6ee930
>
> The only change over the original is the correct initialization of the
> `mSignaled` atomic_bool in WaitListEvent.
>
> Original change's description:
> > [ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent
> >
> > Currently, most futures are implemented using SystemEvent. This includes
> > already completed and non-progressing events. This is problematic on iOS
> > where BrowserEngineKit child processes are not allowed to open fds, mach
> > ports, etc.
> >
> > This CL introduces WaitListEvent which mimics the base::WaitableEvent
> > implementation in Chromium for POSIX platforms. The event internally
> > maintains a list of waiters corresponding to a WaitAny call. In WaitAny,
> > we create a SyncWaiter that's signaled using a condition variable. The
> > waiter is added to each event that the WaitAny is waiting on. The events
> > also have a mutex to allow multiple threads to wait on them. We acquire
> > the event locks in a globally consistent order (sorted by address) to
> > prevent lock order inversion. WaitListEvents can also be waited on
> > asynchronously by returning a SystemEventReceiver which allows mixing
> > waits on SystemEvents and WaitListEvents.
> >
> > In addition, this CL changes how already signaled and non-progressing
> > TrackedEvents are represented. Already signaled events are backed by
> > WaitListEvents and non-progressing events become a flag on TrackedEvent.
> >
> > The code in EventManager is also cleaned up to aid readability and fix
> > an edge case of waiting on multiple queues with zero timeout - we could
> > end up ticking the same queue multiple times causing a subtle race
> > between MapAsync and OnSubmittedWorkDone futures completion.
> >
> > Bug: 407801085

commit.subject: Reland "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent"
commit.message:
Reland "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent"

This is a reland of commit abc42736ef28ed8fcc11e66814907febff6ee930

Original change's description:
> [ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent
>
> Currently, most futures are implemented using SystemEvent. This includes
> already completed and non-progressing events. This is problematic on iOS
> where BrowserEngineKit child processes are not allowed to open fds, mach
> ports, etc.
>
> This CL introduces WaitListEvent which mimics the base::WaitableEvent
> implementation in Chromium for POSIX platforms. The event internally
> maintains a list of waiters corresponding to a WaitAny call. In WaitAny,
> we create a SyncWaiter that's signaled using a condition variable. The
> waiter is added to each event that the WaitAny is waiting on. The events
> also have a mutex to allow multiple threads to wait on them. We acquire
> the event locks in a globally consistent order (sorted by address) to
> prevent lock order inversion. WaitListEvents can also be waited on
> asynchronously by returning a SystemEventReceiver which allows mixing
> waits on SystemEvents and WaitListEvents.
>
> In addition, this CL changes how already signaled and non-progressing
> TrackedEvents are represented. Already signaled events are backed by
> WaitListEvents and non-progressing events become a flag on TrackedEvent.
>
> The code in EventManager is also cleaned up to aid readability and fix
> an edge case of waiting on multiple queues with zero timeout - we could
> end up ticking the same queue multiple times causing a subtle race
> between MapAsync and OnSubmittedWorkDone futures completion.
>
> Bug: 407801085
> Change-Id: I1c5deb8097339be5beb5e9021d753998a074bea3

parents.subject: [BitSet] Make ityp::bitset iterable

commit.subject: [BitSet] Remove BitSetIterator
commit.message:
[BitSet] Remove BitSetIterator

Part of a larger set of changes to update Dawn's BitSet implementation.

Removes BitSetIterator in favor of using ity::bitset (which is now
iterable) everywhere. Simplifies several indirections and reduces copies
of the bitset content.

Bug: 42241557
Change-Id: I5d9867073a866b6c2c2aed1a27f093672cd78a02

commit.message:
[BitSet] Make ityp::bitset iterable

Part of a larger set of changes to update Dawn's BitSet implementation.

This change makes ityp::bitset iterable, moving the
BitSetIterator::Iterator implementation into the ityp::bitset, avoiding
the need for IterateBitSet() and one copy.

parents.subject: [ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent

commit.subject: Revert "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent"
commit.message:
Revert "[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent"

This reverts commit abc42736ef28ed8fcc11e66814907febff6ee930.

Reason for revert: Breaks roll into Skia with both build and UBSan errors:
https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/982121

Bug: 407801085
Original change's description:
> [ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent
>
> Currently, most futures are implemented using SystemEvent. This includes
> already completed and non-progressing events. This is problematic on iOS
> where BrowserEngineKit child processes are not allowed to open fds, mach
> ports, etc.
>
> This CL introduces WaitListEvent which mimics the base::WaitableEvent
> implementation in Chromium for POSIX platforms. The event internally
> maintains a list of waiters corresponding to a WaitAny call. In WaitAny,
> we create a SyncWaiter that's signaled using a condition variable. The
> waiter is added to each event that the WaitAny is waiting on. The events
> also have a mutex to allow multiple threads to wait on them. We acquire
> the event locks in a globally consistent order (sorted by address) to
> prevent lock order inversion. WaitListEvents can also be waited on
> asynchronously by returning a SystemEventReceiver which allows mixing
> waits on SystemEvents and WaitListEvents.
>
> In addition, this CL changes how already signaled and non-progressing
> TrackedEvents are represented. Already signaled events are backed by
> WaitListEvents and non-progressing events become a flag on TrackedEvent.
>
> The code in EventManager is also cleaned up to aid readability and fix
> an edge case of waiting on multiple queues with zero timeout - we could
> end up ticking the same queue multiple times causing a subtle race
> between MapAsync and OnSubmittedWorkDone futures completion.
>
> Bug: 407801085

commit.subject: [ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent
commit.message:
[ios blink] Implement futures using WaitListEvent

Currently, most futures are implemented using SystemEvent. This includes
already completed and non-progressing events. This is problematic on iOS
where BrowserEngineKit child processes are not allowed to open fds, mach
ports, etc.

This CL introduces WaitListEvent which mimics the base::WaitableEvent
implementation in Chromium for POSIX platforms. The event internally
maintains a list of waiters corresponding to a WaitAny call. In WaitAny,
we create a SyncWaiter that's signaled using a condition variable. The
waiter is added to each event that the WaitAny is waiting on. The events
also have a mutex to allow multiple threads to wait on them. We acquire
the event locks in a globally consistent order (sorted by address) to
prevent lock order inversion.

In addition, this CL makes the already completed and non-progressing
TrackedEvents be represented as subtypes of the CompletionData variant.
This allows lazy upgrading to either SystemEvent or WaitListEvent when
waiting on mixed event types. Also, WaitListEvent can be upgraded to a
SystemEvent by adding the SystemEventPipeSender as an async waiter.

The code in EventManager is also cleaned up to aid readability.

Change-Id: I1c5deb8097339be5beb5e9021d753998a074bea3

already completed and non-progressing events. This is problematic on iOS
where BrowserEngineKit child processes are not allowed to open fds, mach
ports, etc.

This CL introduces WaitListEvent which mimics the base::WaitableEvent
implementation in Chromium for POSIX platforms. The event internally
maintains a list of waiters corresponding to a WaitAny call. In WaitAny,
we create a SyncWaiter that's signaled using a condition variable. The
waiter is added to each event that the WaitAny is waiting on. The events
also have a mutex to allow multiple threads to wait on them. We acquire
the event locks in a globally consistent order (sorted by address) to
prevent lock order inversion. WaitListEvents can also be waited on
asynchronously by returning a SystemEventReceiver which allows mixing
waits on SystemEvents and WaitListEvents.

In addition, this CL changes how already signaled and non-progressing
TrackedEvents are represented. Already signaled events are backed by
WaitListEvents and non-progressing events become a flag on TrackedEvent.

The code in EventManager is also cleaned up to aid readability and fix
an edge case of waiting on multiple queues with zero timeout - we could
end up ticking the same queue multiple times causing a subtle race
between MapAsync and OnSubmittedWorkDone futures completion.

commit.subject: Dawn: Use no Tint Program at all in shader compilation cache checking
commit.message:
Dawn: Use no Tint Program at all in shader compilation cache checking

This CL remove Tint Program from all backends' shader compilation cache
key and replace it with SHA3-512 hash of shader module. With this CL,
Tint Program might not be need until actual cache miss in backend shader
compilation or front end WGSL parsing cache miss.

commit.subject: correct Vulkan targets
commit.message:
correct Vulkan targets

Vulkan `VulkanHeadersConfig.cmake` and `VulkanUtilityLibraries-targets.cmake` only adds Vulkan::Headers and Vulkan::UtilityHeaders. Their source `CMakeLists.txt` adds Vulkan-Headers and VulkanUtilityLibraries too, but not when installed in the system.

Change-Id: I8b97a0753907f9534549a8033f6c1341b6ff3513

commit.subject: Range Analysis: Disallow the loop exit conditions that are always true
commit.message:
Range Analysis: Disallow the loop exit conditions that are always true

This patch adds the early-return in function
`GetBinaryToCompareLoopControlVariableInLoopBody()` when the input loop
exit condition is always true for any loop control variable.

e.g.

```
// `i` can be any u32 value instead of just [0u, 100u]
for (var i = 100u; i >= 0u; i--) { ... }
```

Bug: 348701956
Test: tint_unittests
Change-Id: I9cfbd31422cb97850c3a03113d6d0c9098b22343

commit.message:
[tint] Use server mode for E2E tests

Launch a Tint server for each Go test thread. Restart the server when
it exits on failure, crashes, or times out.

This drastically reduces process startup overheads.

commit.subject: Remove SubstittueOverride AST config from Dawn.
commit.message:
Remove SubstittueOverride AST config from Dawn.

The Dawn build was using the AST configuration for SubstituteOverrides
as a way to pass the map around and then converting that to the IR
version later. Instead of passing the AST object around, pass the map
directly which is what we actually need.

Change-Id: I3c9859d529991bfb4a55cd35fb614f764c1e2834

commit.message:
[wgsl] Disallow subgroup matrix in the private address space

The private address space is always considered to be non-uniform,
which means subgroup matrices in var<private> would be unusable
without the diagnostic to disable the uniformity analysis.

commit.subject: DXC build: disable sized allocations
commit.message:
DXC build: disable sized allocations

Chromium will enable this flag by default, which results in ASAN
failures for mismatched new/delete calls in DXC. These are not a
security risk, and haven't been fixed in upstream LLVM either, so let's
disable this flag when building DXC. Note that this is already disabled
for MSVC builds as well (both in our GN build, and in DXC's CMake
build).

Bug: chromium:410141973
Change-Id: Ieccfe2fc49ede3f1cea5ac2ebb15b939c869b0a6

[spirv-reader][ir] Add support for OpAtomicCompareExchange.

Convert the `OpAtomicCompareExchange` instruction into an
`atomicCompareExchangeWeak` in WGSL. The result of the original
expression needs to be extracted and used as the builtin result.

Bug: 391487024
Change-Id: I42c22da639340776dded0094e0bc73c39e5b8522
